note: Codified from the City of San Marcos, TX Development Code, amended January 21, 2025. Conventional SF-6/SF-4.5 from Chapter 4 §§4.4.1.3–4.4.1.4; legacy MU/CC/GC/P/NC/OP from Chapter 9 §9.1.1.1 Dimensional and Development Standards (flipbook pp. 424–425 / code 9:2–9:3) at https://user-3vpeqil.cld.bz/ORD-2025-01-Development-Code-Effective-January-25-2025. Legacy side_corner_ft uses the table Secondary Street minimum. max_height_ft for story-capped districts uses the code footnote (stories may not exceed 14 ft floor-to-ceiling). OMITTED: CD-*, FD, SF-R, ND-*, TH, D, DR, PH-ZL, MF-*, VMU (form/building-type or conditional rules), HC/LI/HI/MH, and PUD/plan districts. OMITTED — ND-3: front setback conditional (15 ft min or Avg); remains honest gap until conditional model exists. LIVE GIS VERIFICATION (2026-09-07, before landing): queried the real zoning layer (smgis.sanmarcostx.gov MPN/MyPermitNowFeatures/6) with an area-weighted group-by on ZONECODE (not raw polygon count, which would be misleading). The two covered current-code districts, SF-6 and SF-4.5, together account for 12.93% of the city's total zoned area. The legacy Chapter 9 residential system this supersedes (D, DR, TH) accounts for 0.90%; SF-11 does not appear in the live layer at all anymore -- every parcel once zoned SF-11 has already been rezoned. Current-code coverage clearly dominates by roughly 14:1, well past the threshold for landing this table as researched. SF-R (2.46% of area) is a separate, small current-code district this research pass does not cover (see OMITTED list above) -- not part of either the covered or legacy figures. P-258 LANE-C ADDENDUM (2026-09-16, acquisition campaign, branch seat/p258-lane-c): 19 districts added from the CURRENT edition of the same Development Code -- ORD-2026-08, effective 2026-06-16, the City's adopted redline PDF republished at sanmarcostx.gov (URL carried as citation_url on every added row). ADDED (Section 4.4.1 conventional residential): FD, SF-R, MH; (4.4.2 neighborhood density): ND-3, ND-3.2, ND-3.5, ND-4, N-CM; (4.4.3 character districts): CD-2, CD-2.5, CD-3, CD-4, CD-5, CD-5D; (4.4.4 special districts): CM, BP, HC, LI, HI. MAPPING: 'Primary/Principal Street' -> front_ft; 'Side' -> side_ft; 'Secondary Street' -> side_corner_ft (the same mapping the legacy Chapter 9 rows above already use); 'Rear' -> rear_ft. READ, DO NOT ASSUME: front/side/corner/rear are read verbatim from each section's 'Setbacks - Principal Building' block; the build-to-zone MAXIMUM figures on CD-4/CD-5/CD-5D/N-CM/CM are NOT setback minimums and are not codified as such (the minimum is). THREE DISTRICTS CARRY A GENUINE NON-SCALAR REAR YARD: FD, SF-R and CD-2 state the rear yard as a PROPORTION of lot depth ('min. 20% of total lot depth measured at the point of the greatest depth'), not feet. rear_ft is coded 100 with not_specified: true and the real rule verbatim in the quote -- a lot-depth proportion cannot be collapsed into a scalar, and the accessory-structure rear figure is a different structure class and was NOT substituted. MH height is stated in STORIES only ('2 stories max.') with no feet figure in Section 4.4.1.5, so max_height_ft is not_specified with the 100 sentinel, matching the established belton-tx.json convention for stories-only districts. max_lot_coverage_pct is the established non-binding 100 sentinel on every added row: the Development Code regulates impervious cover per district and states no separate building-only lot-coverage cap. max_impervious_pct is the ordinance's real per-district figure. VINTAGE CAVEAT (read at source, both values carried rather than one picked): the fetched document is the ADOPTED REDLINE for ORD-2026-08 (effective 2026-06-16), but its internal page footers still read 'Amended: January 21, 2025' because the base pages are the 2025 edition with the 2026 amendments marked up. The added values for SF-6 and SF-4.5 were cross-checked against this file's pre-existing 2025-sourced rows and match exactly (F25/S5/C15/R20 and F20/S5/C15/R15), which is evidence that unchanged text reads as the current text here; any 2026 amendment that changed one of THESE 19 districts' setback cells would not have been distinguished by this extraction, so re-verify against a clean (non-redline) 2026 rendering before treating a cell as finally confirmed. STILL NOT CODED FROM THIS SOURCE, and now carried as named gaps rather than silence: (a) Chapter 9 Legacy Districts (AR, SF-11, MR, D, DR, TH, PH-ZL, MF-12, MF-18, MF-24, VMU, and the P/OP/NC/CC/GC rows already above) -- the adopted-redline PDF stops before Chapter 9, so its Article 1 DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS (9:2) dimensional table was NOT read this pass and no legacy row was touched; (b) CD-1 (Section 4.4.3.1) -- an open-space/preservation district whose section states impervious cover (20% max.) and density (n/a) but NO principal-building setback block at all, so no setback row is written; (c) the PA Planning Area District (4.4.3.8) and the former-SmartCode translation codes (Table 4.9 / SC) -- allocation and translation tables, not per-district setbacks. SOURCES TRIED for the San Marcos units not acquired here: the City's ORD-2026-08 adopted-redline PDF (read, above); the sanitized flipbook edition at user-3vpeqil.cld.bz/ORD-2026-08-Development-Code-Effective-2026-06-16 (table-of-contents page read; the Chapter 9 page was not resolvable to a flipbook page number in this pass); the City of San Marcos DocumentCenter index; and an ArcGIS REST search of the live zoning layer (smgis.sanmarcostx.gov MPN/MyPermitNowFeatures/6) which the earlier rows already cite and which was NOT re-queried this pass.
